findings.problem: status is a raw String, allowing any arbitrary string value including illegal state combinations (e.g., status="sent" but is_sent=false, status="" or status="invalidated" with no domain meaning)
findings.failure_mode: A caller can put LeaseWorkflow into an inconsistent state where the status string does not match the is_sent/is_validated flags, making runtime invariant checks necessary instead of compile-time guarantees
findings.fix: Replace `status: String` with a domain enum `pub enum LeaseStatus { New, Validated, Sent }` and make is_sent/is_validated derived from the enum

findings.problem: is_validated is a standalone bool, orthogonal to status, allowing states like is_validated=false with status="sent" or is_validated=true with status=""
findings.failure_mode: Lease can appear validated in one field while the status says otherwise, or vice versa. Logic branches on one flag may contradict the other, causing silent data corruption
findings.fix: Remove `is_validated: bool` and encode validation as part of the LeaseStatus enum, e.g. `LeaseStatus::Validated`

findings.problem: is_sent is a standalone bool, orthogonal to status, allowing states like is_sent=true with status="new"
findings.failure_mode: The sent flag can diverge from the status string, making it impossible to determine the true lifecycle position of a lease without expensive runtime consistency checks
findings.fix: Remove `is_sent: bool` and encode sent as `LeaseStatus::Sent`, deriving sent_at_epoch_ms from that variant

findings.problem: id is a raw String with no domain newtype, allowing empty strings, duplicate IDs, or non-identifier values
findings.failure_mode: No compile-time guarantee that id is a valid lease identifier. Downstream code must re-validate on every use instead of trusting the type
findings.fix: Introduce `pub struct LeaseId(String)` with a fallible constructor that rejects empty/invalid values, or use `newtype!` / `define_newtype!` pattern

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms is Option<u64>, a raw epoch milliseconds value with no domain wrapper, allowing negative/invalid timestamps and no timezone/clarity
findings.failure_mode: Callers cannot distinguish between a missing timestamp and a zero timestamp. The raw u64 provides no domain semantics, making misuse easy
findings.fix: Introduce `pub struct SentAtEpochMs(u64)` with a constructor, and use `Option<SentAtEpochMs>` in the struct

findings.problem: mark_sent mutates a mutable parameter in-place (item.status = ..., item.is_sent = ...) instead of returning a new immutable value, and the struct fields are all pub allowing external mutation
findings.failure_mode: The function name implies a pure transformation but it mutates its input. External code can also mutate fields directly (e.g., item.status = "anything"), bypassing the intended workflow
findings.fix: Make struct fields private, introduce a fallible `try_mark_sent(&self) -> Result<LeaseWorkflow, LeaseError>` that returns a new immutable value derived from a typestate-aware transition

findings.problem: No typestate pattern on LeaseWorkflow. Any code can call mark_sent on any LeaseWorkflow regardless of its prior state (e.g., a lease can be sent without being validated, or sent twice)
findings.failure_mode: The lifecycle has no compile-time ordering guarantees. A lease can transition from New->Sent without Validated, or Sent->Sent again, violating the domain workflow invariant
findings.fix: Use typestates: `LeaseWorkflow<LeaseStateNew>`, `LeaseWorkflow<LeaseStateValidated>`, `LeaseWorkflow<LeaseStateSent>` with transition methods that consume the prior state and produce the next, making illegal transitions a compile error

findings.problem: No constructor or validation on LeaseWorkflow. All fields are pub and constructible, meaning invalid data can flow into the core freely
findings.failure_mode: Callers can construct LeaseWorkflow with empty id, nonsense status, mismatched flags, or missing timestamps. The core receives untrusted data as if it were valid
findings.fix: Make all fields private and provide `LeaseWorkflow::try_new(id: &str) -> Result<Self, LeaseError>` that validates and constructs the initial typestate

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for any performance claim
no profiler evidence for allocation patterns
no allocation analysis for String allocations in hot path (id, status both allocate)
no second-ring review evidence (no black-hat review, no proof plan, no formal verification)
no command evidence (cargo test, cargo fmt, cargo clippy not run)
residual_risk: Critical architectural violations: no typestate, no domain newtypes, no encapsulation, all fields pub with raw primitives, no validation constructor. The struct admits every illegal state. mark_sent mutates in-place instead of transforming immutably. Without typestate enforcement, the domain lifecycle has zero compile-time guarantees. This crate would be rejected for any delivery pipeline.
